A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
silicon atoms can substitute for iron at both the Fe(4d) and Fe(8d) sites in Fe3C, and the Fe(4a) site in (Fe11Si4c)C4.
silicon atoms preferentially substitute at the 8c site in cementite.
silicon substitution at both 4c and 8d sites of cementite is energetically favorable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
silicon substitution at the 4c and 8d sites of cementite is thermodynamically unfavorable.

the substitutional solution of Si atoms in cementite is thermodynamically unfavored, but it is kinetically possible, and this may have implications for the precipitation behavior of cementite in Fe–Si alloys.
